Title: Diagnosis

Details: The failing test is checking the density value of a MultivariateNormalDistribution for a one-dimensional case with mean 0 and variance 1, expecting approximately 0.398942280401433. The issue report notes that density returns wrong value when the dimension is odd.

Looking into the density method of MultivariateNormalDistribution, we see that it calculates the density as:

```
FastMath.pow(2 * FastMath.PI, -dim / 2) * FastMath.pow(covarianceMatrixDeterminant, -0.5) * getExponentTerm(vals)
```

Note that `dim` is an integer (the dimension of the input vector). The expression `-dim / 2` does integer division, so for example if `dim` is 1 (an odd dimension), `-dim / 2` equals 0 in integer division, leading to `FastMath.pow(2 * FastMath.PI, 0)` which equals 1. This is incorrect because in the formula for the normal distribution the exponent should be `-dim/2.0` as a double division to correctly yield fractional exponents.

This explains why the density calculation is incorrect for odd dimensions. The exponent should be floating-point division rather than integer division.

The `getExponentTerm` method and other parts seem correctly implemented. The root cause is the integer division in the density method on line 183.

Thus the bug is caused by treating `dim` as an integer in the power expression, leading to wrong density results when `dim` is odd.

The fix should convert `dim` to double or use `-dim / 2.0` to ensure floating-point division in the density method.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
